items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Robo Show, did he feature much jazz at all in his band? ... No I wouldn't because he was strictly a straight-filing man

ctx.x: Yeah, I used to play at the Lyric Theater. I used to go there all the time. Midnight shows? Before I left. Yeah, they used to have midnight shows. That was before I left New Orleans, way back there. I was here around 22, 23, 24. I started left in 27. Well now, Robo Show, did he feature much jazz at all in his band? About stuff started off like a march, then they, along the middle part of it, they started ragtime and jazz and that's how they played the Overtube, but after that they just played the Showdown.
So he did have some men that could play jazz in his band. Oh yeah, yeah. Would you call him a hot man, Robichaud himself?
No I wouldn't because he was strictly a straight-filing man, you know. He played by ear at all? Yeah, he must have did.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Well Robichaud and Tuxedo did a lot of reading.

ctx.x: But who had the straight bands, you know, straight reading bands other than.
Well Robichaud and Tuxedo did a lot of reading. But after that, them other fellows, they weren't doing much reading. This Desveen fellow too, he had a nice reading band.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: The biggest band it was was Robichaud had the lyrics.

ctx.x: The biggest band it was was Robichaud had the lyrics. And he's using two trumpets, two clarinets, two trombones, piano.
Do you remember when Celestan started having a saxophone?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1958-05-24
items.q: I seen him at the Regal Theater there with Robichoke Bay.

ctx.x: Goldston, yeah. Now, really happy. He was a real good drummer and everything, but I never did play with him. You know, I seen him at the Regal Theater there with Robichoke Bay. I thought he was a mighty good drummer. I thought he was a very good drummer. I thought he was a very good drummer.

I never met him. I heard Paul Balberin talk a lot about him. One of his favorites is not his favorite. Well, what did John McMurray play like? Isn't that his name? Mac Murray, they called it. I'm not sure of his first name. Did you know him? Mac Murray, the drummer. Did you ever know him? No. I never knew him.
